correctness.rationale: The corrected proof checks the three sufficient configurations, including p0,p1,p2 by explicit forces followed by the basis action and duality. A monochromatic set lacking such a triple lies on one line or through one point; in a mixed set lacking a nonincident pair, two distinct selected lines force the selected points into their singleton intersection, and a single selected line supplies its own star. From any full star the observation step leaves four unseen vertices on the opposite shore; every observed vertex has zero or at least two unobserved neighbors. Monotonicity gives failure of all its subsets. Distinct stars intersect in at most two vertices, so no triple is overcounted. Failed pairs are 21 incidences plus 42 same-shore pairs, and the failed triples and four-sets number 56 and 14. The fresh independent enumeration constructed the incidence model, started each of all 16,384 masks at its closed neighborhood, iterated unique-neighbor forcing to a fixed point and compared failure against star containment. It reproduced the entire failure vector, and incidentally confirmed the frozen exchange statistics. The original supplied verification scripts were inspected rather than executed. No general projective-plane classification of larger sets or formal verification is claimed.

value.rationale: For this canonical cubic graph the natural obstruction invariant specifies robustness against any placement, not merely the best pair or a total count. It supplies a short geometry-based criterion, identifies every maximal failure, explains exact counts by cardinality, and shows the sharp size threshold for guaranteed success. The distinction between placements of equal size without a successful pair is substantive and does not follow mechanically from the covered mobility result.
